landing.heroBody: Find universities that fit your profile, discover scholarships, understand your application strength, and turn a complicated admissions process into a clear plan.
landing.enterApp: Already have a profile? Enter the app
landing.howText: Your academic record, tests, activities, goals, budget and preferences become the foundation for every recommendation.
landing.step1Text: Bring your academics, tests, activities, awards, projects and goals into one place.
landing.step2Text: Explore universities and scholarships matched to your actual profile and constraints.
landing.step3Text: Get deadlines, documents, application tasks and personalized priorities in one roadmap.
landing.step4Text: Track applications, improve essays, check documents and prepare for interviews.
landing.featText: ScholarBridge brings discovery, preparation and application management into one connected experience.
landing.f1Text: Compare academic fit, tuition, living costs, requirements, location and other profile-specific factors.
landing.f2Text: Keep university fit separate from admission estimates — transparent data-basis labels, and no invented probabilities.
landing.f3Text: Discover opportunities based on eligibility, degree, profile, award value, deadlines and requirements.
landing.f4Text: Ask questions about your application and receive grounded guidance without invented facts or guarantees.
landing.f5Text: Keep applications, tasks, deadlines and documents organized from one dashboard.
landing.f6Text: Turn your profile gaps and upcoming deadlines into prioritized next actions.
landing.chanceTitle: Fit and chance are not the same thing.
landing.chanceText: A university can be a great fit without being easy to get into. ScholarBridge keeps those concepts separate and explains the evidence behind an estimate.
landing.chanceLi2: Admission estimates are shown only when outcome evidence supports them, with the data basis named explicitly.
landing.chanceLi3: As ScholarBridge collects consented application outcomes, the evidence layer becomes richer over time.
landing.chanceNote: Admission probability is shown only when the available evidence supports an estimate. The platform intentionally does not invent a probability.
landing.roadTitle: Stop wondering what to do next.
landing.roadText: ScholarBridge turns your application journey into prioritized actions — from missing tests and documents to essays, scholarships and deadlines.
landing.r1Text: See missing required documents, expiring credentials and other issues that can stop an application.
landing.r2Text: Identify meaningful gaps across academics, English, activities, projects and application materials.
landing.r3Text: Prioritize the tasks that matter most based on urgency, impact and your application timeline.
landing.quote: The goal isn't to make a student chase a number. It's to help them understand their options, see the evidence, and know what to do next.
landing.ctaText: Create one profile and let ScholarBridge organize the universities, scholarships, applications and next steps around you.
landing.footerLeft: ScholarBridge AI — built to make admissions clearer.
landing.mockPortfolioNote: Tiers describe fit, not your chance of admission. Evidence-based labels only — never an invented number.
landing.mockHubSub: Matching your academic credentials (GPA 4.7/5) for Bachelor in Computer Science across top universities.

help.title: What is this page?
help.dashboard: Start here. "Your path" shows the 8 steps of studying abroad and highlights the one to do now. Below are your progress and quick links.
help.universities: Search universities by country, subject and cost. Press the bookmark to save a university — saved ones feed your fit check and applications.
help.scholarships: All scholarships in one list. Use filters, open the official site, and save the ones you want to apply for.
help.chancing: See how your profile compares with each saved university's published requirements: Reach (fit is a stretch), Match, Safety (comfortably met). It is a requirements-fit estimate, not a promise of admission.
help.strength: Shows how complete and strong your profile is and what to improve first.
help.similar: Admitted students whose grades and goals look like yours — see where they got in.
help.stories: Real stories from admitted students, checked by our team. The top ones are the most similar to you. You can share your own story too.
help.autopilot: Scholarships that match your profile, sorted by what to do first. For each one press: Save, I applied, or Not for me. We never apply for you.
help.vault: Common application questions. Write each answer once — it saves automatically — then copy it into any form.
help.goals: Pick up to 6 goals (for example IELTS 7.0 or a volunteering project) and tick the steps as you go. Fewer goals, done well, beat many half-done ones.
help.departure: Got an offer? Go through these steps from accepting the offer to your first week abroad. Tick each item when it is done.
help.planning: Plan your budget, scholarship portfolio and CV in one place.
help.applications: Every application in one list with its status and deadline.
help.sop: Write and improve your statement of purpose and essays with AI feedback.
help.tasks: Your personal timeline: what to do this week and what is coming next.
help.chat: Ask the AI mentor any question about studying abroad. Check important facts on the official site.
help.visa: Practise common visa interview questions out loud and get feedback.
help.forum: Ask questions and share tips with other students.
help.rewards: Invite friends and earn points and rewards.
help.notifications: Connect our Telegram bot once: you can then sign in with a code instead of a password, and deadline, scholarship and security alerts reach your phone. You decide which alerts to get.
help.study-plan: Your plan and your tests in one place. The plan updates itself from your real data — tests, documents, applications and funding — so a test date and the task that prepares for it never drift apart.
help.profile: Everything universities see: readiness by area, your goals, activities and stories. A readiness score describes your inputs — it never guarantees admission.
help.funding: Plan the money before you apply: the full yearly cost, your budget, funding you already have, and the gap that is left. Every number shows whether it is an estimate or unknown.
help.materials: The reusable material behind every application: requirements with their sources, documents and saved answers, essays and recommendations, and interview practice.
help.offers: Record what each university decided. Offers, funding and the visa steps stay connected, so accepting one does not lose the rest.
help.post-admission-funding: What you must pay after an offer — deposits and instalments — and the funding that covers them. It reuses the same budget as your Financial Plan.
help.guidance: AI guidance and human consulting, clearly separated. AI answers are a study aid, not an official admissions decision.
help.community: Discussions with other students and structured courses with certificates.

growthSeed.g0d: Most scholarships ask for IELTS 6.5–7.0. A clear 8-week plan beats random practice.
growthSeed.g0s0: Take a full mock test to find your band
growthSeed.g0s1: Pick your weakest skill and practise it 4× a week
growthSeed.g0s2: Do 2 timed Writing Task 2 essays per week and get feedback
growthSeed.g0s4: Take a final mock 1 week before
growthSeed.g1d: Admissions officers look at the trend. One strong semester can change the story.
growthSeed.g1s0: List every course and your current grade
growthSeed.g1s1: Choose 2 courses to improve by one grade
growthSeed.g1s2: Book weekly office hours / tutor time
growthSeed.g2t: Start a club or community project
growthSeed.g2d: Founding something small and real shows initiative more than joining ten clubs.
growthSeed.g2s0: Pick a problem you care about in your school or mahalla
growthSeed.g2s2: Run the first event or session
growthSeed.g2s3: Measure the impact (people reached, hours, money raised)
growthSeed.g3d: National olympiads, hackathons and essay contests are strong, verifiable achievements.
growthSeed.g3s0: Choose one competition that fits your major
growthSeed.g3s4: Add the result to your profile
growthSeed.g4d: A finished project (app, research poster, design set) you can link in applications.
growthSeed.g4s0: Pick a project you can finish in 6 weeks
growthSeed.g4s3: Ask a teacher or mentor for feedback
growthSeed.g5d: Helps with interviews, visa appointments and leadership roles.
growthSeed.g5s1: Present once in class or a club
growthSeed.g5s2: Do 3 mock interviews in Visa Speaking
growthSeed.g5s3: Give one talk to a bigger audience
growthSeed.g6d: Ask early — teachers write better letters when they have time.
growthSeed.g6s0: Choose 2 teachers who know your work
growthSeed.g6s2: Ask in person and give the deadline
growthSeed.g6s3: Send a thank-you note after submission
growthSeed.g7t: Do a summer programme or internship
growthSeed.g7d: Real experience in your field makes your essays and interviews concrete.
growthSeed.g7s1: Prepare CV and short motivation letter
growthSeed.g7s3: Plan what you want to learn and document it
growthSeed.p0h: Who you are, where you come from and what drives you — in plain words.
growthSeed.p1q: Why do you want to study this subject?
growthSeed.p1h: One real moment that made you choose it beats a list of adjectives.
growthSeed.p2q: Why do you want to study abroad?
growthSeed.p2h: What you cannot get at home and what you will bring back.
growthSeed.p3q: What are your career goals after graduation?
growthSeed.p3h: Short-term (first job) and long-term (10 years). Connect them to your country.
growthSeed.p4q: Describe a time you showed leadership.
growthSeed.p4h: Situation → what YOU did → result with a number if possible.
growthSeed.p5h: Focus on what you learned and how you changed, not only the problem.
growthSeed.p6q: How have you contributed to your community?
growthSeed.p6h: Volunteering, helping family, teaching others — small and real counts.
growthSeed.p7h: Pick one, explain why it matters to you.
growthSeed.c0d: Put total cost, scholarship and job prospects side by side before deciding.
growthSeed.c1t: Accept one offer and pay the deposit
growthSeed.c1d: Note the acceptance deadline — offers expire.
growthSeed.c2d: Frees the place for another student and keeps a good record.
growthSeed.c3t: Get your CAS / I-20 / admission letter
growthSeed.c3d: The university issues it after you accept — you need it for the visa.
growthSeed.c4d: Appointment slots in Tashkent can fill up weeks ahead.
growthSeed.c6d: Bank statement or sponsor letter covering tuition + living costs for the required period.
growthSeed.c7d: Visa/Mastercard that works abroad for the first weeks.
growthSeed.c8d: University halls open applications right after you accept.
growthSeed.c9d: Arrive a few days before orientation week.
growthSeed.c10d: Many countries require it for the visa or on arrival.
growthSeed.c11d: Passport, visa, offer letter, diplomas — paper + cloud copy.
growthSeed.c12t: Register with the university and local authorities
growthSeed.c12d: Some countries require police/residence registration within days of arrival.
growthSeed.c13t: Get a local SIM card and open a bank account

adminOwnership.title: Platform ownership
adminOwnership.intro: The owner is the highest role inside ScholarBridge. Only the owner appoints admins and transfers ownership to another admin. External accounts (hosting, bot, AI) are not transferred automatically — see the checklist below.
adminOwnership.notOwner: You are an admin, not the owner
adminOwnership.noOwner: No owner yet (there is no administrator).
adminOwnership.startIntro: The new owner must be an existing admin. They accept with their password, then you confirm with yours. The offer expires after {hours} hours.
adminOwnership.retainAdmin: Keep my admin access after the transfer
adminOwnership.waitingTarget: Waiting for the new owner to accept.
adminOwnership.waitingOwner: Accepted — the current owner must confirm.
adminOwnership.confirmHint: Ownership moves immediately when you confirm.
adminOwnership.acceptHint: You were offered ownership of this platform. After you accept, the current owner confirms the transfer.
adminOwnership.adminsIntro: Only the owner grants or removes admin access. Every change is audited.
adminOwnership.checklistIntro: The app only transfers in-app ownership. These external accounts must be moved manually.

app_owner.label: Platform owner role
app_owner.detail: Moves to the new owner when the transfer is confirmed.

admin_access.label: Admin access
admin_access.detail: The new owner is (and stays) an admin; the previous owner keeps admin only if chosen.

ai_keys.label: AI provider accounts & billing
ai_keys.detail: Keys saved in Admin → AI keep working but belong to the previous owner's provider accounts. The new owner should create their own keys and replace them (rotation), then the old ones should be revoked at the provider.

telegram_bot.label: Telegram bot
telegram_bot.detail: Manual Telegram ownership transfer may be required: in @BotFather use /mybots → Bot Settings → Transfer Ownership (Telegram requirements apply), or create a new bot and replace TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN.

hosting.label: Hosting (e.g. Render/Vercel)
hosting.detail: Transfer the service/project or redeploy under the new owner's account and copy the environment variables.

database.label: Database / Supabase project
database.detail: Transfer the project to the new owner's organisation (or migrate the data).

domain.label: Domain & DNS
domain.detail: Move the domain registrar account or update DNS; then set APP_URL and re-register the Telegram webhook.

payments.label: Payment merchant accounts
payments.detail: Payme/Click merchant contracts are legal agreements and are not transferred by the app.

secrets.label: Secrets
secrets.detail: Rotate SESSION_SECRET (signs everyone out), CRON_SECRET, TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and AI_KEYS_ENCRYPTION_SECRET (keep the old one in AI_KEYS_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_PREVIOUS, then re-encrypt keys).

search_console.label: Google Search Console
search_console.detail: Add the new owner as an owner of the property; update GOOGLE_SITE_VERIFICATION if needed.

recommend.title: Program Recommender
recommend.subtitle: Programs from the university catalog, matched to what you want to study. Subject fit, published requirements, affordability and funding are assessed as four separate dimensions — nothing is filled in from memory.
recommend.whyText: Only your fields of interest are required. Every other field is optional: adding it makes the match more precise, and skipping it never hurts you. Missing data is shown as “unknown” and is never counted against you.
recommend.prefilledNote: Prefilled from your saved profile. Edit or clear any field before running the match.
recommend.interestsHint: Choose up to five areas or specializations. You can also say you’re still exploring.
recommend.degreeLevelWhy: Optional — weighs programs at your level (Bachelor, Master, PhD…).
recommend.gpaWhy: Optional — compared with published program minimums. Enter the scale you use (4, 5, 100). Without a scale, a GPA above 4 is treated as unknown.
recommend.testsWhy: Optional — used only when a program publishes a minimum score.
recommend.countriesWhy: Optional — programs in these countries get a small ranking bonus. It never hides other countries.
recommend.budgetWhy: Optional — marks programs as within/over your budget. Tuition published in another currency is shown as unknown, never converted.
recommend.fundingWhy: Optional — need-based scholarship matches are shown only when you choose this.
recommend.languagePrefWhy: Optional — programs taught in this language rank slightly higher.
recommend.startYearWhy: Optional — used only to label the application cycle. It never filters results.
recommend.errorAuth: Please sign in to use the recommender.
recommend.errorInterests: Choose at least one interest or select “I’m still exploring.”

hubs.introUniversities: Find where you could study. Start from a subject or a career, or from a university you already have in mind. Program fit, eligibility, affordability and admission outlook are always shown separately — never merged into one score.
hubs.introScholarships: One place for funding. Browse the catalog or open the queue matched to your profile — every recommendation says why it matched, what you meet and what is unknown. Nothing is submitted for you.
hubs.introStudyPlan: Your plan and your tests together, so a test date and the task that prepares for it can never drift apart.
hubs.introTasks: Everything with a date in one timeline: what it is, why it matters, when it is due, and the page where you do it.
hubs.introProfile: What universities see, and what to improve next. A readiness score describes your inputs — it never guarantees admission.
hubs.introFunding: Plan the money before you apply: the full yearly cost, your budget, funding you already have, and the gap that is left.
hubs.introApplications: One tracker and one workspace per application: status, progress, next deadline and the next useful action.
hubs.introMaterials: The reusable material behind every application: requirements, documents, saved answers, essays, recommendations and interview practice.
hubs.introOffers: Record what each university decided and work through the decision, without losing the funding or visa work that follows it.
hubs.introPostAdmissionFunding: What you must pay after an offer — deposits and instalments — and the funding that covers them. It reuses the same budget as your Financial Plan.
hubs.introVisa: The visa case first, then the practical steps after it: documents, interview, flight, housing, insurance and arrival.
hubs.introGuidance: AI guidance and human consulting, kept clearly apart. AI answers are a study aid — not an official admissions decision, and never a guarantee.
hubs.introCommunity: Talk to other students who are doing this now, and take structured courses that end with a certificate.
hubs.noApplicationHint: Choose an application above, or start one from My Applications. Your documents, saved answers and essays are shared, so you never enter anything twice.
hubs.noApplicationsYet: You have not started an application yet
hubs.noApplicationsHint: Save a program you like, then start an application from My Applications — your profile, documents and answers come with it.
hubs.offersEmptyHint: After Admission is ready before you hear back: record offers here when they arrive, and see what each one asks of you.
hubs.afterAdmissionNote: You can read these pages now — they become useful the moment you have an offer. Nothing here is decided for you.
hubs.aiDisclaimer: AI guidance is a study aid. It is not an official admissions authority and cannot guarantee an outcome.
hubs.premiumPaneNote: This tab is part of Premium. Everything else on this page stays free.
hubs.outlookExplain: Admission outlook is shown next to the requirements it comes from. It describes how your profile compares with published requirements — it is never a probability and never a guarantee.

disclaimers.general: ScholarBridgeAI is an independent guide — it is not affiliated with any university, scholarship provider or government. AI output and catalogue data can be wrong or out of date; always confirm the details at the official source.
disclaimers.ai: AI-assisted result. AI can be wrong, incomplete or invent details — treat it as a study aid, never as an official decision or a guarantee. Check anything important with the university or the official source.
disclaimers.catalogue: Reference data — tuition, costs, rankings, deadlines and requirements — is compiled from public sources and may be out of date. Confirm every number on the official university or scholarship page before you rely on it.
disclaimers.estimate: This is an estimate, not a prediction. Scores and chances describe your inputs and the available evidence; nobody can guarantee an offer, a scholarship or a visa.
disclaimers.money: Amounts are estimates. Tuition, living costs, exchange rates and funding change — verify the current figures with the university or provider before you pay or commit.
disclaimers.planning: This plan is built from what you entered. It is a suggestion, not an official requirement or deadline — always check each university's own website.
disclaimers.visa: Visa and immigration rules change often and depend on your personal case. This is not legal advice — the official embassy or immigration website makes the decision.
disclaimers.community: Community content is written by other students. It is not verified advice and may be wrong — treat it as a starting point, not a fact.
disclaimers.thirdParty: Mentors, courses and payment providers are independent third parties. ScholarBridgeAI does not operate their services — check their terms, refunds and prices before you pay.
disclaimers.prototype: Prototype build: some data and features are incomplete and can change without notice. Do not treat this as a final source.
disclaimers.certificate: Certificates are issued by ScholarBridgeAI for completing its own courses. They are not university credits or an accredited qualification.
